about: Functional groups of the MaleCNS ROIs (colour, decision type), plain names and short explanations per ROI, and plain descriptions of cell-type families. Scientific ROI names follow Ito et al. 2014 and the MaleCNS/MANC nomenclature. Shared by the web app, the share cards and the server-rendered pages.

groups.name: Mushroom body

kind.title: Memory Call
kind.line: She dug through her memories before deciding.

groups.about: The fly's learning and memory centre. About 2,000 Kenyon cells store which smells and sights meant sugar or trouble.

groups.name: Antennal lobe

kind.title: Sniff Test
kind.line: She smelled her way to this one.

groups.about: The smell centre. Every scent the antennae pick up lands here first.

groups.name: Lateral horn
groups.about: Inborn reactions to smells, no learning needed: ripe fruit means come closer, rot means go away.

groups.name: Central complex

kind.title: True North
kind.line: She set a course and stuck to it.

groups.about: The fly's navigation system: a compass, a speedometer and a route planner in the middle of the brain.

groups.name: Optic lobe

kind.title: Eye Witness
kind.line: She went with what she could see.

groups.about: The eyes' own computer. It turns light from 800 tiny lenses per eye into edges, colours and motion.

groups.name: Visual hubs

kind.title: Lookout
kind.line: She kept an eye on what's coming.

groups.about: Where sights get meaning: landmarks, the sky, and things heading straight for her.

groups.name: Hearing centres
groups.about: A fly hears with her antennae. These centres decode wind, gravity, sound and love songs.

groups.name: Superior protocerebrum

kind.title: Deep Thought
kind.line: She weighed it all up, properly.

groups.about: The thinking cap on top of the brain. It weighs hunger, mood and past rewards against what's on offer.

groups.name: Gnathal ganglion

kind.title: Sweet Tooth
kind.line: Her taste buds had the final say.

groups.about: Taste, eating and grooming. It decides whether something goes in the mouth.

groups.name: Premotor centres

kind.title: Full Speed Ahead
kind.line: Her body moved before she'd finished thinking.

groups.about: Where decisions become movement: turn left, turn right, take off, run.

groups.name: Leg centres

kind.title: Itchy Feet
kind.line: Her legs were ready to go.

groups.about: In the nerve cord, the fly's spinal cord. Six legs for walking, grooming and tasting with her feet.

groups.name: Wing and neck centres
groups.about: In the nerve cord: flight, balance and the wing songs male flies sing.

groups.name: Abdominal ganglion

kind.title: Butterflies
kind.line: She felt this one in her tummy.

groups.about: The back end of the nerve cord: belly, digestion and mating.

CA.about: Smell signals arrive here and are handed to the memory cells.

PED.about: The stalk that carries the memory cells' fibres from the inbox to the lobes.

gL.about: Known for short-term memory: which smell meant sugar a few minutes ago.

a'L.about: Helps learn something new and hold on to it for the first few hours.

b'L.about: Helps learn something new and hold on to it for the first few hours.

aL.about: Needed to recall memories that last for days.

bL.about: Needed to recall memories that last for days.

AL.about: Smells are sorted into about 50 tiny balls here, one for each kind of smell receptor.

LH.about: Inborn reactions to smells: ripe fruit, come closer. Rot, go away.

EB.about: A ring of neurons that works like a compass needle, tracking which way she's facing.

FB.about: Picks where to head next, and helps decide when it's time to sleep.

PB.about: A row of 18 little boxes that maps every direction she could fly.

NO.about: Tracks how fast she's moving, so she can count her way back home.

AB.about: A small, lopsided structure, bigger on one side. Scientists are still working out what it does.

ME.about: The eye's main computer: edges, colours and motion from about 800 little lenses.

LO.about: Picks out shapes and small moving things, like another fly.

LOP.about: Senses which way the world slides past, to keep her flight straight.

LA.about: Where light from the eye turns into nerve signals.

AME.about: Home of the internal clock that tells her when it's morning.

AOTU.about: Reads the sky's light pattern and landmarks and passes them to the compass.

BU.about: Feeds what the sky and landmarks look like into the compass ring.

PVLP.about: Watches for things rushing closer, like a hand or a swatter.

PLP.about: Mixes what the eyes see with where she's going.

SAD.about: Where the antennae report sound, wind and gravity.

WED.about: Works out where the wind and sounds are coming from.

AVLP.about: Decodes sounds and sights, including the songs flies sing when they court.

SMP.about: Weighs hunger, thirst and mood against what's on offer.

SIP.about: Hears from the memory centre whether something felt good last time.

SLP.about: Decides whether a smell means food, a mate or danger.

CRE.about: Where memory signals meet steering commands.

SCL.about: A wiring hub around the memory lobes that links senses to actions.

ICL.about: A wiring hub around the memory lobes that links senses to actions.

IB.about: Links the two halves of the brain for seeing and steering.

ATL.about: A small antler-shaped hub next to the compass. Its job is only partly understood.

GNG.about: Taste, feeding and grooming: decides whether food goes in.

PRW.about: Runs swallowing and the taste sensors inside the mouth.

FLA.about: Where neurons that release hormones into the body send their signals.

LAL.about: Turns the brain's decisions into left and right turns.

VES.about: Passes commands from the brain down to the body.

SPS.about: Uses what the eyes see to keep head and flight steady.

IPS.about: Keeps the head level while the body moves.

EPA.about: A small relay between seeing and moving.

GOR.about: A small relay that passes commands towards the neck.

CAN.about: A small relay near the neck. Barely studied so far.

CV-anterior.about: The neck cable that carries commands from the brain to the body.

CV-posterior.about: The neck cable's nerve-cord end, carrying news from the body up to the brain.

CRN.about: Feels how the head is tilted on the neck.

LegNp(T1).about: Walking, grooming and tasting: flies taste with their front feet.

LegNp(T2).about: Walking, and the jump that launches every take-off.

LegNp(T3).about: Walking, and brushing the wings clean.

mVAC(T1).about: Collects touch from the bristles on the front legs.

mVAC(T2).about: Collects touch from the bristles on the middle legs.

mVAC(T3).about: Collects touch from the bristles on the hind legs.

WTct(UTct-T2).about: Drives the wings: flying, and the songs male flies sing.

HTct(UTct-T3).about: Runs the halteres, two tiny knobs behind the wings that work like a gyroscope.

IntTct.about: Keeps wings and legs in step, for example at take-off.

LTct.about: Links legs and wings for the escape jump.

Ov.about: A small hub in the nerve cord that collects signals from leg and wing sensors.

ANm.about: Runs the belly: digestion, and mating.
